name: Rainbow Countdown
tagline: The rainbow timer every class already watches, caught mid-countdown on the amber board.
concept: The icon is the app's signature widget: the cream timer face inside a thick rainbow ring with round caps. The ring has run down by a little over a quarter, so the pale spent track shows as a clear gap at the upper-left, which is exactly where the real ring empties first, and the face carries a big Poppins-style 5 in the app's warm-gray-800 (#3d3835). It sits on the real amber low-poly canvas (#cf923f to #9c5f27, lit from the top-left, with a soft warm shadow falling down-right), which beat deep sage because it is the board teachers actually project. A white die-cut rim borrowed from the stickers gives every hue of the deepened, OKLCH-blended spectrum (red at twelve through orange, gold, lime, teal and blue to violet) luminance contrast against both the plate and the face, so figure/ground never rests on hue alone. The gap is the single asymmetric feature, with no hands, ticks or hub, so it reads as a draining timer rather than a clock, and only two focal elements (ring and numeral) sit on the calm frame; the glyph is the same drawing (the same 260-degree round-capped arc and the identical stroked 5), so the menu-bar item is the colour icon with the colour taken out.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it is a bold C-ring open at the upper-left around a heavy 5 (ring 112 units, numeral strokes 110, every counter and the ring clearance at least 100), reading as a countdown with time already gone rather than the text clock beside it, a spinner or a record dot. A 5 was chosen over the screenshot's 6 because a 6's diagonal stem crosses the ring centre and turns into a clock hand at menu-bar size.

name: Runner on the Ring
tagline: The Timer's own hamster, caught mid-stride as it springs off the rainbow ring every class watches run down.
concept: The hero is the Timer's default runner, a chunky golden hamster, caught mid-stride as its hind paw pushes off the inside of the app's rainbow ring while the ring depletes behind it (the spent segment a pale sage track at ten-to-twelve), which is exactly the frame the running timer shows. Every colour is lifted from the live board: the ring's own left-to-right rainbow (red at the depleting end, green at twelve and six, violet at three), the cream timer face, the amber low-poly canvas, and a cream die-cut bezel borrowed from the stickers that also gives the red/orange arc a luminance edge against the amber; brand sage appears only in the calm depleted track. The hamster wears the app creatures' style (gold fur, cream chin-to-belly bib, pink ears, dark paws, brown cartoon outline), lit from the top-left with soft warm grey-green shadows, keeping three focal elements (runner, ring, face) and no text. Icon and glyph are one geometry: the glyph is the 290-degree ring arc plus the hamster silhouette traced from the same distance field, joined at the planted foot into one closed mass, and the colour icon is that exact drawing scaled 0.705 into the plate with fur, face and bezel layered on.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it reads as a bold ring with a gap at ten-to-twelve and a round-eared critter springing off its lower-left inside; with no hands or ticks it cannot pass for the menu-bar clock, and the ears, snout and gallop are the asymmetric hook (at @2x the ears, snout, front paw and tail separate cleanly). One closed mass of #000 fills: ring 112 units, every limb, ear and tail at least 111, clearance to the ring at least 104, verified with raster opening/closing tests.

name: Name Drop
tagline: The moment the randomiser lands on a name: a white chip glows in the purple-pink-amber slot as confetti pops off the card.
concept: This is the randomiser at the instant it lands. The cream widget card holds the slot window in the app's own gradient (Tailwind purple-400 → pink-400 → yellow-400). It is laid out with the same geometry CSS uses for to-br, so it runs pink from corner to corner exactly as it does on the board. The chosen name is a bright white rounded-lg chip, and the neighbouring names peek in faded and slightly motion-blurred from the window edges, like a reel that has just stopped. Two folded-paper confetti flecks in the real react-confetti-explosion colours pop off the card's top edge, where the app fires its burst. Yellow #FFC700 is lighter and navy #2E3191 darker than the plate, so both separate by luminance, not hue. The plate is the amber low-poly canvas every widget sits on, lit from the top-left with soft warm-brown shadows. There is one hero (the card and its white chip) and one accent (the confetti pair). Nothing depends on telling red from green, and it holds up in greyscale and at 16px as a pink card with a white bar. The glyph is the same geometry at 1.25×: the card's silhouette with the chosen chip knocked out, and the same two flecks at the same angles, so the colour icon is the glyph filled in. The idea also animates: the reel spins as a loading state and the flecks burst as the success animation.
glyphNotes: At 18pt it reads as a solid wide card with a bright slot (the picked name) and two confetti flecks rising off its top edge: a dash low on the left and a diamond high on the right. That asymmetric pair is what stops it reading as minus.rectangle.fill, a battery or a printer, and it has no hands, ticks, grid or speech bubble. Every solid shape is at least 118 units thick and every gap at least 114 (the flecks are 170 apart), so the slot and both flecks stay separate pixels even at 16px white on dark.

name: Ring & Reel
tagline: The rainbow countdown ring floats in front of the name-picker card on the amber board: the two widgets every teacher reaches for, drawn the way the class sees them.
concept: Ring & Reel shows the app's two most-used widgets the way they actually sit on a projected board. The timer's rainbow ring floats in front of the corner of the randomiser card, with a gap that grows back from 12 o'clock exactly as the real timer runs down and a bold "5" on its cream face. The card's slot window holds the chosen name pill between two faded neighbours. Recognition comes from the app's real colours: the plate is the amber low-poly canvas (#dea24f to #a2602a), the ring uses the timer's own left-to-right rainbow gradient, the slot uses the purple, pink and amber gradient sampled from the widget, and the surfaces are the widgets' cream. Warm brown shadows fall from a single top-left light. There are only two focal elements, and the timer is clearly the hero because it sits in front, is fully saturated and carries the numeral. The glyph is the same drawing reduced to ink: the rainbow arc becomes a 114-unit ring with the identical open gap, the card becomes a solid rounded card with the chosen pill knocked out, and a 100-unit knockout ring takes the place of the timer's shadow. The colour icon leaves the spent track open rather than grey, so icon and glyph share the same silhouette at every size. Only the numeral is icon-only, because it would be too fine at 18 px.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it reads as a thick C-ring, notched at 10 to 12 o'clock like a timer mid-countdown, overlapping the corner of a solid card with a pill-shaped window. Every stroke is at least 110 units and every gap at least 100, so the notch, the pill and the knockout band each stay about 2 px wide, and with no hands, ticks or hub it cannot be confused with the menu-bar clock or any system symbol.

name: Gold Star Timer
tagline: Classroom Widgets' own die-cut star sticker, slapped onto its rainbow countdown timer.
concept: The icon is one of the app's own stickers. It uses the sticker widget's chunky rounded star (the Font Awesome solid star in orange-500, lighter at the centre) with a thick white die-cut border, rounded inner corners and a soft drop shadow. The star is tilted 14° and slapped onto the cream face of the signature timer, so it hangs over the rim onto the board. A teacher sees the two things they use every lesson, so it reads as "the thing with the rainbow timer" rather than abstract tiles: the rainbow countdown ring and a sticker. The ring uses the app's real horizontal gradient (red at left, green at 12 o'clock, blue-violet at right), drawn clockwise from 12 with round caps and a pale used-up track at upper-left. The colours are the product's own. The plate is the caramel low-poly canvas (#d49a4a→#9e6127 with faint facets) and the widget is the app's cream. The only saturated notes are the rainbow and the orange star, lit from the top-left with warm-brown shadows and no highlight bars. The glyph is the same layout at 1024: the timer ring drops to the one allowed 50% tone as a depleting arc and the star sits solid on top, so overlap and tone do the die-cut's job, because a 100-unit knockout gap would have broken the ring into a crescent-and-star shape at 18 px.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it reads as a solid star stuck over a half-tone timer ring, and the small gap at upper-left says "counting down". It is two closed masses (a 128-unit ring and a 199-unit gap between the ring's caps), and every star tip either lands at least 39 units inside the ring or clears it by at least 136, so nothing is tangent. The star hanging over the lower-right is the asymmetric feature, and there are no hands, ticks, dots or crescent to clash with the menu-bar clock or system icons.

name: Mini Board
tagline: The Classroom Widgets board in one glance: the rainbow countdown, the name-picker card behind it, and a star sticker slapped where they meet.
concept: A thumbnail of the screen teachers actually project. The hero is the rainbow timer: a cream disc with a big dark 6, the arc running clockwise from a round red cap at 12 o'clock through the rainbow, and the pale depleted track at the upper left, just as the app runs down. Behind it sits the randomiser card: cream frame, purple→pink→amber slot, faint side pills and the bright white chosen-name pill. An orange die-cut star with a thick white border and a slight tilt is slapped over the join, and a burst of the app's red, yellow, teal and navy confetti flies off the card. Every hue is lifted from the product and sits on the low-poly amber canvas, with cream surfaces, soft deep-sage-tinted shadows and one top-left light, so the brand palette stays the calm frame. The glyph is the same three-piece board translated by luminance: the vivid parts (rainbow arc, star) go solid; the soft parts (depleted track, pastel card) share the single 50% tone. Every overlap becomes a 100-unit knockout, playing the part of the sticker's white border: a notch concentric with the timer where it sits in front of the card, and a cut around the star that the ring and card both tuck under.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it reads as a progress ring (a solid arc starting with a flush seam at 12 o'clock, plus a half-tone depleted track) with a chunky star biting its 9 o'clock edge and a half-tone card tucked behind at top left. It has no hands, ticks or hub dot, so it can't be mistaken for the menu-bar clock. The track needs the 0.5 tone, because without it the arc reads as a hook, and the card shares that tone to sit behind. It is three closed masses: a 132-unit ring and knockouts of at least 100 units, all corners rounded to at least 56, and star tips rounded to 88 units across, checked with a disc-kernel test.
direction: A mini board — timer, card, sticker

name: The Confetti Moment
tagline: The name picker lands on a student and the board bursts into confetti, the moment every class cheers.
concept: The mark is the Randomiser at the moment it lands: the real cream slot card with its lavender, pink and amber window and three name pills, the chosen one bright white. Chunky confetti fans out of the card's top-right corner. It uses the app's own colours, sampled from the screenshots: the canvas amber (#cb8f3e to #8a5326, with faint low-poly facets, so the plate is the board), the cream widget surface, the slot gradient (#cc9ff7, #f28fce, #fcd262) and the real confetti colours (red, #ffc700 yellow, #41bbc7 teal, #2e3191 navy), with brand terracotta as a seventh accent. Red nearly matches the amber in luminance (L* 53 vs 51), so each piece has a soft warm shadow that grows with its height, and the plate is darkened behind the burst. A faint warm glow sits where the confetti pops, and the light falls consistently from the top-left. The icon has three focal elements: the card as hero, the burst, and the board. The glyph is the same drawing reduced to ink. The same master coordinates, scaled 0.78 into the plate, place the card, the chosen-name slot and the three big strips (red, yellow, teal) in both. The icon only adds the window, the faded pills, two navy dots and a terracotta fleck.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as a card with a centred name slot and three paper strips tumbling from its top-right corner. The strips sit at 23°, 110° (leaning back over the card) and 54°, so they read as confetti rather than shine rays, a sun or a "new" burst, and nothing resembles a clock, screen or chat bubble. It is four closed masses: strips 124 units wide, card rim 116 beside the slot and 167 above and below it, slot 136, and gaps between pieces of at least 103 (checked by computing clearances); the bounding box is centred.

name: Widget Bento
tagline: The launcher grid teachers already know, now filled with the real widgets they project every day: the rainbow timer, the name picker, the traffic light and a star sticker.
concept: The old 3×3 launcher grid is cut into a bento of four compartments, each sized to a real widget's natural shape. The rainbow timer takes the big square top-left cell as the clear hero, the traffic light stands in a tall pill, the randomiser fills a wide card, and a tilted star sticker sits in the last cell. Each cell copies the live app, so a teacher reads it as "the thing with the rainbow timer and the name picker". The ring runs clockwise from 12 to 9 o'clock over the pale depleted track, with the app's soft glow and a bold 6 on the cream face. The slot window uses the app's purple→pink→amber gradient, with the chosen name in a white pill between faded neighbours on the reel, and the star has its white die-cut border. The plate is the app's own amber low-poly canvas. The cream widget surfaces, one top-left light and soft warm grey-green shadows keep four bright widgets calm rather than garish. The icon draws its widgets inside a single matrix(0.74) group from exactly the glyph's coordinates: ring arc = rainbow arc, ring notch = depleted track, pill hole = lit green lamp, card slot = chosen-name pill, star = sticker outline. So the colour icon is the glyph with its widgets filled in.
glyphNotes: At 18px it reads as four different small objects locked in a calm grid: a C-shaped ring with a clear notch at upper-left, a tall pill with one hole, a wide slab with a slot, and a stubby tilted star. It has no hands, ticks or matching tiles, so it cannot pass for the clock, an app grid or the Windows logo. Strokes and walls are 110 units or more (ring 136), and gaps and knockouts are 100 or more (gutters 104, ring notch 141, star clearance 108+, ring hole 256), with no islands or hairlines.

name: Great-Job Timer
tagline: The rainbow timer mid-countdown, with a teacher's heart sticker slapped on its rim.
concept: A flat, poster-style close-up of two things found on every Classroom Widgets board: the rainbow timer mid-countdown (cream face, big 5, the pale elapsed track opening at the top right) and a die-cut heart sticker slapped over its rim at a tilt, riding the ring's leading edge where the app's runner creature would be. The colours are the app's own. The rainbow uses the timer's own stops on a linear axis, rotated so the visible arc runs the full spectrum from red at lower left to a blue end cap. The cream face keeps a warmed version of the app's grey track, and the sticker is Tailwind pink-500 with the app's white die-cut edge and soft drop shadow, all on the amber low-poly canvas with three faint facets. There is one top-left light (a lighter plate, face and sticker highlight toward the upper left, warm olive-brown shadows falling down-right) and only two focal elements, with the timer as the hero; confetti was tested and dropped because at dock size it only added specks. The glyph is the same drawing in one colour: the solid ring is the time left, the single 50% arc is the pale elapsed track, and the 100-unit knockout around the heart is the sticker's white die-cut border.
glyphNotes: At 18 px it reads as a thick timer ring (135 units) with a lighter elapsed segment at the upper right and a chunky heart (about 440 units) breaking the rim at four o'clock behind a 100-unit knockout. It is one closed ring-plus-heart silhouette with no hands, ticks or arrowheads, so it cannot pass for the menu-bar clock, a sync or refresh arrow, or a record dot; it was checked at 16, 18 and 36 px on light and dark bars.
